observations.why: Flat unhedged assertion of a historical fact — asserted and defensible but carrying no ratification language or operational rule that would lift it to decision.

Framing onboarding as checklist completion appeals to keeping what works (conservation) and mastery of required steps (competence), but no value is named or plainly appealed to — the motive is structural, not voiced.

Replacement of an old system with a newer one could gesture toward openness-to-change, but the text frames it as a routine update — no novelty or stimulation is appealed to; the value signal is too thin to commit.
Domain jargon deployed natively and instrumentally — checklist items listed flatly with no glossing, establishing the document's prevailing register as technical-matter-of-fact.
Flat instrumental update with a temporal anchor and no performance — consistent with the baseline established in src-1, not a departure from it.
